mc.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes genotype and phenotype?
mc.answer: Genotype is the allele combination; phenotype is the measured characteristic
mc.explanation: Allele combinations and expressed characteristics are different levels of description.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: Genotype is the allele combination; phenotype is the measured characteristic
Genotype is always colour; phenotype is always DNA sequence

mc.prompt: A recessive allele is rare in one population and common in another. Is this inconsistent with recessiveness?
mc.answer: No; dominance does not determine allele frequency
mc.explanation: Dominance concerns the heterozygote, not how common an allele is.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: No; because dominant alleles never affect phenotype
No; dominance does not determine allele frequency
Yes; recessive alleles must always be rare
Yes; frequency changes turn it into a chromosome

Dominant alleles vanish after one generation

writing.model: The heterozygote produces B or b gametes and bb produces b. The combinations are Bb and bb, each with probability 1/2. Therefore the expected genotype ratio is 1:1 and the expected dominant-to-recessive phenotype ratio is also 1:1.

writing.model: The count is an expectation from a 1/4 probability multiplied by 100. Individual gamete combinations are chance events, so the observed count can differ. The model predicts a distribution of possibilities rather than an exact scheduled sequence.

mc.prompt: Five dominant offspring appear in a test cross. What is the most careful conclusion?
mc.answer: Homozygosity is supported, but heterozygosity is not logically excluded
mc.explanation: A finite run of dominant offspring can occur by chance from a heterozygote.

options: The recessive allele has mutated into A in every cell

mc.prompt: A dominant-phenotype individual has an aa parent. Under the simple model, its genotype is:

mc.explanation: The aa parent must supply a; the dominant phenotype requires A from the other parent.

writing.prompt: Explain why a recessive tester makes an unknown dominant genotype easier to investigate.
writing.model: The homozygous recessive tester contributes only the recessive allele. Offspring outcomes therefore reveal whether the unknown parent can contribute a recessive allele. A recessive offspring identifies the unknown dominant parent as heterozygous within the model.

writing.model: Each offspring has probability 1/2 of the dominant phenotype. Four specified independent outcomes have probability (1/2)⁴ = 1/16. Thus an all-dominant sample of four can occur even when the unknown parent is heterozygous.

mc.explanation: P(aa) = 1/4 and P(B_) = 3/4, giving 3/16.

writing.model: Type A is IAIA or IAi, type B is IBIB or IBi, type AB is IAIB, and type O is ii. IA and IB are codominant with one another and each is dominant over i.

writing.model: The type O parent supplied i, so the type A individual is IAi. The partner is ii. IAi × ii produces IAi and ii with equal probability, giving expected type A and type O offspring in a 1:1 ratio.

mc.prompt: Which relationship contradicts a simple fully penetrant X-linked dominant model with an affected father?
mc.answer: An unaffected daughter under the stated ordinary transmission assumptions
mc.explanation: Every daughter should inherit the affected paternal X under the model.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: An unaffected daughter under the stated ordinary transmission assumptions

mc.prompt: An unaffected mother has an affected son in a simple X-linked recessive model with no new mutation. What is inferred?
mc.answer: She is a carrier
mc.explanation: She supplied the son’s affected X but has an unaffected phenotype, so a second unaffected allele is present.

Every daughter must also be affected

writing.model: The transmission route can create required or impossible allele contributions under a model. Unequal sex counts alone can occur by chance in a small family. Checking every parent–offspring relationship provides stronger evidence than relying on one superficial pattern.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In a completely dominant, single-locus model, which cross predicts a 3:1 dominant-to-recessive phenotype ratio?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The four equally likely outcomes are AA, Aa, Aa and aa. A sample ratio is evidence, not an exact guarantee.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A double heterozygote carries linked alleles in the phase GT/gt. What can produce Gt and gT gametes?
practiceQuestions.answer: Crossing over between the two loci
options: Crossing over between the two loci
Independent segregation of alleles on an unchanged same chromosome
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A crossover between loci can exchange chromosome segments and form nonparental allele combinations.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A test cross is used to determine
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A recessive tester helps distinguish the possible genotypes behind a dominant phenotype; sample size affects certainty when no recessive offspring appear.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Assume independent assortment and complete dominance at both loci. What phenotype ratio is predicted for TtYy × TtYy?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Each locus predicts a 3:1 phenotype ratio. Multiplying independent probabilities gives 9/16, 3/16, 3/16 and 1/16.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Tallness T is completely dominant to t. Flower alleles R1/R2 show incomplete dominance, with heterozygotes pink. What offspring result from TTR1R1 × ttR2R2?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Each parent supplies only one gamete type; heterozygosity has different phenotype rules at the two loci.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A heterozygote is tall for one trait but intermediate pink for another. Which inheritance description fits the stated model?
practiceQuestions.answer: Complete dominance for height and incomplete dominance for colour
options: Complete dominance for height and incomplete dominance for colour
Codominance for height and Y linkage for colour
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Dominance relationships must be evaluated separately at each locus.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In a hypothetical single-locus trait, B is dominant to b. An individual with the dominant phenotype has a recessive-phenotype child with a bb partner. What is the first parent’s genotype?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The recessive child is bb and must receive b from both parents; the dominant-phenotype parent must also carry B.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Under a fully penetrant autosomal-recessive model, two unaffected carriers have a child. What is the probability the child is affected?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Aa × Aa predicts aa in one of four equally likely genotype combinations. Earlier births do not change this probability.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In an explicitly additive model with equally contributing loci and no environmental variation, AABBCC is crossed with aabbcc. What is predicted?
practiceQuestions.answer: All AaBbCc offspring with an intermediate model value
options: All AaBbCc offspring with an intermediate model value
Every offspring has either extreme parental genotype
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: All F1 offspring receive the same intermediate number of contributing alleles in this simplified additive model.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In a fully penetrant autosomal-dominant model, two affected parents have an unaffected child. What must both parents be?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An unaffected child is aa; both affected parents must be able to supply a, making each Aa.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A model has red homozygotes, white homozygotes and pink heterozygotes. What inheritance relationship is shown?
options: Codominance with separate red and white patches
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The heterozygous phenotype is intermediate under the specified model.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In persons with sickle-cell disease, the red blood cells are shaped like a “sickle” and are not biconcave disks like normal red blood cells. Mr. and Mrs. Charleson are both carriers ( Hb A Hb S ) of sickle-cell disease. What are the chances of their having a child with sickle-cell disease?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: For HbA/HbS × HbA/HbS, the HbS/HbS combination has probability 1/4 in each conception under the stated model.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Two independent completely dominant loci have parental genotypes AABB × aabb. What describes the F1?
practiceQuestions.answer: All AaBb with both dominant phenotypes
options: All AaBb with both dominant phenotypes
Four phenotype classes in a 1:1:1:1 ratio
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Only AB and ab parental gametes are available, producing identical heterozygous combinations at these loci.

practiceQuestions.prompt: For independent AaBb × AaBb, what is the probability of the dominant A phenotype together with bb?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: P(A_) = 3/4 and P(bb) = 1/4; their product is 3/16.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In a fully penetrant recessive model, an aa mother has an affected daughter and an unaffected son. What must their father’s genotype be?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The father supplies a to the affected child and A to the unaffected child, so he carries both alleles.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A heterozygous affected parent Aa and an unaffected parent aa have offspring in a fully penetrant dominant model. What affected probability is predicted?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Aa × aa gives one-half Aa and one-half aa. The statement is conditional on the inheritance model.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The feather colour in some species of chickens is governed by two dominant alleles (co-dominance). practiceQuestions.answer: 100 percent of the chicks will have black and white plumage.
options: 100 percent of the chicks will have black and white plumage.
50 percent of the chicks will have black and white plumage, and 50 percent of the chicks will have grey plumage.
50 percent of the chicks will have black plumage and 50 percent of the chicks will have white plumage.
100 percent of the chicks will have grey plumage.
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: BB × WW gives all BW offspring; with codominance both products are expressed rather than an intermediate grey phenotype.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In fruit flies the gene for eye colour is found on the X chromosome. In these flies, red eye colour is dominant to white-eye colour. Predict the probability of producing white-eyed male offspring in a cross between a female fly that is homozygous for red eye colour and a male fly that has white eyes.
practiceQuestions.answer: 0 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
options: 100 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
0 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
75 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
25 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.

practiceQuestions.explanation: Every son receives a dominant red-eye X from the homozygous mother and a Y from the father, so none is white-eyed in this model.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Assume independent assortment and complete dominance. What phenotype ratio is predicted for RrPp × rrpp?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The double heterozygote forms RP, Rp, rP and rp gametes equally; the tester forms rp only.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In the standard ABO model, what is the probability of type A from IAi × IAi?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: IAIA and IAi produce type A; ii produces O. Three of four combinations are type A.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A test cross yields 420 parental and 80 recombinant offspring. What is the approximate short-interval map distance?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Recombination frequency is 80/(420 + 80) × 100 = 16%, corresponding to about 16 cM in the stated approximation.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A carrier mother XAXa and unaffected father XAY have a son. Under a fully penetrant X-linked recessive model, what is the probability that this son is affected?
practiceQuestions.cue: Identify the relevant mechanism or quantity and apply the stated model.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Conditioning on a son leaves XAY and XaY equally likely. The all-children affected probability would instead be 1/4.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A DNA sequence that contributes to a functional product or inherited characteristic.

practiceQuestions.explanation: A DNA sequence that contributes to a functional product or inherited characteristic. A gene and a particular version of that gene are different concepts.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? An alternative version of a gene.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An alternative version of a gene. A diploid individual usually carries two alleles at an autosomal locus, even when more exist in the population.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The allele combination an organism carries at the locus or loci being considered.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The allele combination an organism carries at the locus or loci being considered. Genotype records the allele combination, not just the appearance.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? An observable or measurable characteristic resulting from genotype and its biological context.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An observable or measurable characteristic resulting from genotype and its biological context. Phenotypes can include physiological or behavioural traits, not only colour.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The separation of the two alleles at a locus into different gametes.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The separation of the two alleles at a locus into different gametes. The parent has both alleles, but an individual gamete receives one.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Producing offspring with the same trait when bred within the line under the stated conditions.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Producing offspring with the same trait when bred within the line under the stated conditions. In Mendel’s simple models, true-breeding lines are homozygous for the studied trait.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The first offspring generation from a specified parental cross.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The first offspring generation from a specified parental cross. F1 names a relationship to a cross, not a universal genotype.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The generation produced from the F1 in the specified breeding design.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The generation produced from the F1 in the specified breeding design. Its ratios depend on the parental genotypes and assumptions.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A table combining possible parental gametes to organize offspring genotypes.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A table combining possible parental gametes to organize offspring genotypes. Each cell represents a possible combination, not a separate guaranteed offspring.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A cross between individuals heterozygous for one studied gene.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A cross between individuals heterozygous for one studied gene. A single-trait cross is not always heterozygote × heterozygote.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The expected proportion of an outcome under specified conditions.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The expected proportion of an outcome under specified conditions. Use the group asked about as the denominator.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The predicted count obtained by multiplying a probability by the sample size.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The predicted count obtained by multiplying a probability by the sample size. An expected count need not equal an observed count.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A cross with a homozygous recessive individual used to investigate an unknown genotype.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A cross with a homozygous recessive individual used to investigate an unknown genotype. One recessive offspring can be informative; all dominant offspring in a small sample need not prove homozygosity.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Having two identical alleles at a locus.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Having two identical alleles at a locus. Homozygous can be dominant or recessive.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Having two different alleles at a locus.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Having two different alleles at a locus. A heterozygote can share a phenotype with a homozygous dominant individual.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Differences between observed sample outcomes and their expected proportions due to chance.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Differences between observed sample outcomes and their expected proportions due to chance. A small sample may not distinguish two models decisively.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A cross between individuals heterozygous at two studied loci.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A cross between individuals heterozygous at two studied loci. The familiar 9:3:3:1 phenotype ratio needs complete dominance and independent assortment.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Independent segregation of alleles at different loci when the chromosome arrangement permits it.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Independent segregation of alleles at different loci when the chromosome arrangement permits it. Linked genes can depart from this equal-combination prediction.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Multiplication of probabilities for specified independent events.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Multiplication of probabilities for specified independent events. Check independence before multiplying separate trait probabilities.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The set of one allele from each studied locus carried by a gamete.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The set of one allele from each studied locus carried by a gamete. A gamete does not receive both A and a at the same autosomal locus in this model.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? An allele relationship in which the heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An allele relationship in which the heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype. An intermediate phenotype does not mean the alleles permanently blend.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? An allele relationship in which both allele-associated products or traits are expressed in a heterozygote.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An allele relationship in which both allele-associated products or traits are expressed in a heterozygote. Codominance is not limited to separate patches of cells; both products can be present in the same cells.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The characteristic expressed when two different alleles occur together.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The characteristic expressed when two different alleles occur together. The same notation does not establish the inheritance relationship without its definition.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The expected relative proportions of expressed trait categories.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The expected relative proportions of expressed trait categories. Phenotype ratios can change even when genotype segregation is unchanged.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? More than two allele versions of one gene present in a population.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: More than two allele versions of one gene present in a population. An individual still usually carries only two alleles at that autosomal locus.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A blood-group system modeled with IA, IB and i alleles producing A, B, AB and O phenotypes.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A blood-group system modeled with IA, IB and i alleles producing A, B, AB and O phenotypes. The classroom model omits rare variants and is not a transfusion decision tool.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Alleles whose contributions are both expressed in the heterozygote.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Alleles whose contributions are both expressed in the heterozygote. Both are dominant over i in the simplified ABO model.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? An individual who carries a recessive disease-associated allele without expressing the recessive condition in a specified simple model.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An individual who carries a recessive disease-associated allele without expressing the recessive condition in a specified simple model. Use carrier only when the inheritance model and trait make the meaning appropriate.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Located on the X chromosome.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Located on the X chromosome. An XY individual has only one allele at many X-linked loci.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Having only one copy of a gene in the relevant chromosome context.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Having only one copy of a gene in the relevant chromosome context. Hemizygous is not the same as homozygous.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Probability calculated within a stated subgroup or condition.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Probability calculated within a stated subgroup or condition. Changing the denominator can change the numerical answer.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? An inheritance model in which the recessive allele is on X and is expressed in a hemizygous XY individual.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An inheritance model in which the recessive allele is on X and is expressed in a hemizygous XY individual. An affected father does not transmit his X to sons in the typical XX/XY model.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Inheritance in which multiple genes contribute to a trait.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Inheritance in which multiple genes contribute to a trait. Polygenic does not mean many alleles at only one locus.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A range of phenotype values without only a few sharply separated categories.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A range of phenotype values without only a few sharply separated categories. Continuous measurements can reflect both genetic and environmental contributions.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? An effect of conditions such as nutrition or temperature on phenotype.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An effect of conditions such as nutrition or temperature on phenotype. An environmental effect does not necessarily change the inherited DNA sequence.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Use of genetic information to produce functional products in cells.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Use of genetic information to produce functional products in cells. Expression can change without changing the allele sequence.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A diagram tracing a specified trait through family relationships across generations.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A diagram tracing a specified trait through family relationships across generations. A pedigree is evidence to test a model, not proof that one clue is always decisive.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A model in which a trait is expressed when two recessive alleles occur at an autosomal locus.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A model in which a trait is expressed when two recessive alleles occur at an autosomal locus. Unaffected individuals can be AA or Aa.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A model in which one dominant allele at an autosomal locus is sufficient for expression under the stated assumptions.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A model in which one dominant allele at an autosomal locus is sufficient for expression under the stated assumptions. Affected individuals can be DD or Dd unless other evidence resolves the genotype.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A level of descent in a family diagram, commonly labelled with a Roman numeral.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A level of descent in a family diagram, commonly labelled with a Roman numeral. Individual numbers identify people within a generation.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A simple model in which a dominant allele on X produces the trait under specified penetrance assumptions.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A simple model in which a dominant allele on X produces the trait under specified penetrance assumptions. No direct paternal X is transmitted to a son.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The proportion of individuals with a genotype who express the associated phenotype.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The proportion of individuals with a genotype who express the associated phenotype. Incomplete penetrance can make patterns less straightforward than classroom models.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A possible inheritance explanation tested against the observed relationships and traits.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A possible inheritance explanation tested against the observed relationships and traits. A model consistent with a small family need not be the only possible explanation.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? An individual who must carry a recessive allele under the stated pedigree model.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An individual who must carry a recessive allele under the stated pedigree model. The conclusion depends on the model and relationship information.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Genes on the same chromosome that may be inherited together, especially when close.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Genes on the same chromosome that may be inherited together, especially when close. Physical linkage can reduce recombinant frequency, but widely separated loci may appear independent.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? An allele combination matching one of the original chromosome arrangements in the heterozygous parent.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An allele combination matching one of the original chromosome arrangements in the heterozygous parent. Parental depends on the specified phase, not always capital letters together.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? An allele combination different from the parent’s original arrangement for the loci considered.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: An allele combination different from the parent’s original arrangement for the loci considered. Recombinant does not necessarily mean a new allele was created.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The arrangement of alleles across the two homologous chromosomes.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The arrangement of alleles across the two homologous chromosomes. The compact genotype AaBb alone does not specify phase.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? The fraction of scored offspring or gametes that are recombinant for the loci considered.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The fraction of scored offspring or gametes that are recombinant for the loci considered. Use all scored offspring in the denominator and both recombinant classes in the numerator.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A unit of genetic map distance corresponding approximately to one percent recombination over short intervals.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A unit of genetic map distance corresponding approximately to one percent recombination over short intervals. A map unit is not a universal fixed number of base pairs.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A map of relative gene order and distances estimated from recombination data.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A map of relative gene order and distances estimated from recombination data. A genetic map is not a direct microscopic measurement of DNA length.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Two exchange events within a chromosome region.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Two exchange events within a chromosome region. Undetected multiple crossovers can make observed two-locus recombination underestimate longer distances.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Analysis of genetic material or related markers to investigate particular variants or conditions.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Analysis of genetic material or related markers to investigate particular variants or conditions. A test’s scope determines what a negative or positive result can establish.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A process helping people understand genetic information, inheritance and possible implications for their choices.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A process helping people understand genetic information, inheritance and possible implications for their choices. Counselling supports informed decisions rather than dictating one choice for every family.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? Agreement based on understanding the purpose, potential benefits, risks and alternatives of a procedure or study.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Agreement based on understanding the purpose, potential benefits, risks and alternatives of a procedure or study. Consent involves more than the physical act of giving a sample.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which term matches this description? A probability or increased likelihood associated with genetic information in a specified context.
practiceQuestions.cue: Use the meaning of each term, not the length of its name.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A probability or increased likelihood associated with genetic information in a specified context. Risk is not the same as certainty.

videos.title: Test crosses and unknown genotypes — video support
videos.purpose: Use a homozygous recessive tester to distinguish possible parental genotypes and explain uncertainty from small samples.
videos.fallback: One aa offspring from B_ × bb means the dominant-phenotype parent must carry the recessive allele, assuming the model, parentage and observations are correct. It is heterozygous. By contrast, several dominant offspring do not logically prove the parent is homozygous. An Aa parent can, by chance, produce a run of A-bearing gametes. For four independent offspring in an Aa × aa cross, the probability that all show the dominant phenotype is (1/2)⁴ = 1/16. More offspring with no recessive phenotype generally strengthen the homozygous interpretation, but finite samples still require cautious wording. Say what the evidence supports and what remains possible.
videos.availability: Source hyperlink resolved syntactically; external playback not certified.

videos.title: Single-trait crosses and probability — video support
videos.purpose: Construct and interpret a monohybrid Punnett square, distinguish genotype and phenotype probabilities, and state the denominator.
videos.fallback: For Aa × Aa, the four equally likely combinations are AA, Aa, aA and aa. Grouping the two heterozygous combinations gives probabilities of 1/4 AA, 1/2 Aa and 1/4 aa. The dominant phenotype has probability 3/4 under complete dominance. Genotype probability and phenotype probability therefore can differ. “Heterozygous” refers to two of the four combinations, while “dominant phenotype” includes three. Mark the requested group before choosing your numerator. When converting to an expected number, multiply by the total. If 80 offspring each have a 1/4 chance of aa, the expected number is 80 × 0.25 = 20. The result is an expectation, not a promise.

videos.title: Two-trait crosses and independent assortment — video support
videos.purpose: List valid gametes for two loci, use a Punnett square or product rule, and identify the assumption of independent assortment.
videos.fallback: For AaBb × AaBb, the A locus gives a 3/4 dominant-phenotype probability and 1/4 recessive probability. The B locus gives the same. If the loci assort independently, the probability of both dominant phenotypes is 3/4 × 3/4 = 9/16. The other phenotype combinations are 3/16, 3/16 and 1/16, producing the familiar 9:3:3:1 expectation. This ratio is specific to the stated heterozygote cross and allele relationships. For a different cross, recompute. In AaBb × aaBb, probability of A_ is 1/2 and probability of B_ is 3/4, so both dominant phenotypes have probability 3/8. A memorized 9/16 would be wrong.

videos.title: Sex-linked inheritance — video support
videos.purpose: Use a typical XX/XY model to solve X-linked crosses and distinguish conditional from joint probabilities.
videos.fallback: Consider XBXb × XBY. The four equally likely combinations are XBXB, XBXb, XBY and XbY. One of four children is expected to be affected. Among sons only, one of two is expected to be affected. The probability of “a son who is affected” is 1/4 among all children. The probability that “the next son is affected” is 1/2 conditional on being a son. The wording changes the denominator, not the biological cross. An affected father passes his X chromosome to daughters and his Y to sons in this model. Father-to-son transmission therefore is not expected for an X-linked allele through that direct chromosome path.

videos.title: Multiple alleles and ABO blood groups — video support
videos.purpose: Use the ABO model to distinguish population allele diversity from individual genotype and solve blood-group crosses.
videos.fallback: Type A can be IAIA or IAi. Type B can be IBIB or IBi. Type AB is IAIB, and type O is ii in the standard model. The phenotypes A and B leave genotype uncertainty unless additional family information is available. An individual with type B and a type O parent must have inherited i from that parent. Therefore the type B individual's genotype is IBi. This is the same constraint reasoning used in a test cross. Use clear notation. IAIB represents two alleles of one gene, not four separate genes. In plain text, write IA and IB consistently and keep the allele pairs grouped.

videos.title: Reading autosomal pedigrees — video support
videos.purpose: Read pedigree symbols and generations, infer autosomal genotypes under a stated model, and preserve unresolved alternatives.
videos.fallback: For an autosomal recessive model, affected individuals are aa. Two unaffected parents with an affected child must each contribute a. If both are unaffected, each is therefore Aa under the simple fully penetrant model. For an autosomal dominant model, unaffected individuals are dd. An affected parent with an unaffected child must be able to contribute d, so that affected parent is Dd rather than DD. The child's genotype constrains the parent's possible alleles. These deductions use the stated model, accurate relationships and complete expression. New mutations, reduced penetrance or other complexities can change the interpretation; do not add them silently to a simple problem.

videos.title: Sex-linked pedigrees and testing a model — video support
videos.purpose: Use chromosome transmission to evaluate X-linked models and distinguish consistency from proof in small pedigrees.
videos.fallback: An affected father in an X-linked dominant model passes the affected X to every daughter. With an unaffected mother, sons receive the father's Y and the mother's unaffected X, so they are unaffected under that model. For X-linked recessive inheritance, an affected father with a homozygous unaffected mother has carrier daughters and unaffected sons. The same chromosome route produces a different expressed pattern because the heterozygote phenotype differs. More affected males can be a clue to an X-linked recessive model, but sex counts alone are not decisive. A small autosomal family can also show an uneven distribution by chance.

videos.title: Polygenic traits and environmental influences — video support
videos.purpose: Explain polygenic and environmental contributions, and distinguish genotype, gene expression and measured phenotype.
videos.fallback: Nutrition, temperature and other conditions can influence a phenotype. Plants with similar genotypes may reach different heights under different light or nutrient conditions. The measured difference does not automatically establish a difference in DNA sequence. Gene expression describes which genetic information is used and how much product is made. Cells with the same inherited genome can have different functions because they express different sets of genes. Environmental or developmental signals can change expression. Some regulatory changes involve chemical modifications associated with DNA or chromatin. These are often discussed as epigenetic changes. Do not treat every such change as a mutation or assume it is always inherited through many generations.

videos.title: Linked genes and recombinant offspring — video support
videos.purpose: Identify linked allele arrangements, parental and recombinant combinations, and use a test cross to interpret gamete frequencies.
videos.fallback: Cross a heterozygote with aabb. The tester contributes only ab, so the offspring's phenotype or genotype can reveal the heterozygote's gamete contribution. Under independent assortment, the four combinations are expected in equal proportions. If the heterozygote has AB/ab and the genes are linked, AB and ab gametes often occur more frequently than Ab and aB. The corresponding parental offspring classes are larger, and the recombinant classes smaller. Read the actual counts, not just the presence of four categories. Linked genes can produce all four combinations if crossing over occurs, but the proportions can differ from 1:1:1:1.

videos.title: Recombination frequency and chromosome maps — video support
videos.purpose: Calculate recombination frequency, construct simple maps and distinguish map distance from a universal physical base-pair distance.
videos.fallback: Suppose A–B is 6 map units, B–C is 14 and A–C is 20 in a simple additive map. Since 6 + 14 = 20, B lies between A and C. Either A—6—B—14—C or its reversed orientation expresses the same relative order. Two distances alone may leave more than one order possible. Place the genes tentatively and ask what additional comparison would distinguish the alternatives. Do not invent a third distance merely to finish the drawing.
